name: CA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Harder holds a massive cash advantage: $4.7M on hand versus McBride's $19K
District leans Democratic by eight points and Harder is the incumbent
Prediction markets price Harder's win odds at 96-98%
No public polls or expert ratings are available to test the fundamentals
model.rationale: Harder's overwhelming financial edge, the district's eight-point Democratic lean, and markets pricing his win odds near ninety-seven percent all point to a safe hold; with no polling available, fundamentals carry the forecast.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Harder or a sharply nationalized environment could narrow the margin, though the money gap limits McBride's ability to capitalize.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Josh Harder, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a district that leans Democratic by about eight points on the partisan index. He faces Republican John McBride, who has run a minimal campaign financially. Harder has raised more than four million dollars and holds nearly five million on hand, while McBride has raised roughly fifty thousand with under twenty thousand available. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters are tracking the race.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket price Harder's chances at roughly ninety-six to ninety-eight percent, consistent with the district's lean and his incumbency and financial advantage. The combination of partisan lean, incumbency, and an overwhelming money gap makes an upset unlikely, though the absence of polling leaves some residual uncertainty. The race is rated Safe Democratic.
